text:
**Short version:** Qi2 and Qi2.2 are open standards from the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC), and MagSafe is Apple's own branded version of the same idea. Qi2.2 is the faster update to Qi2.

| | Qi2 | Qi2.2 (Qi2 25W) | MagSafe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who | WPC (open standard) | WPC (open standard) | Apple |
| Max speed | 15W | 25W | 15W for most iPhones, up to 25W on newer ones |
| Magnets | Yes | Yes | Yes |

**Qi2:** This is the first Qi standard with a magnetic ring, which aligns the phone and charger for faster, more efficient charging. It was built with contributions from Apple's MagSafe tech and tops out at 15W ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)).

**Qi2.2:** The WPC officially calls it Qi v2.2.1, branded "Qi2 25W." It launched in July 2025 with nearly 70% more power than Qi2. The WPC says it can take a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**MagSafe:** This is Apple's brand, supported on iPhone 12 and later except the SE and 16e. Apple-certified accessories also include an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify them, plus a magnetometer to prevent compass interference. "MagSafe-compatible" chargers that aren't certified are usually just 7.5W with a ring of magnets ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)). Apple's current MagSafe Charger is itself certified for Qi2 25W, so the two overlap now.

**Your phone sets the real speed:**
- **25W:** iPhone 17 series, 16 Plus and 16 Pro Max, with a 30W or greater adapter.
- **22.5W:** iPhone 16 and 16 Pro.
- **20W:** iPhone Air.
- **15W:** iPhone 15 and earlier, and the 17e.
- **None:** The iPhone 16e has no MagSafe or Qi2 charging.

(Source: [Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047).)

On Android, the Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold support Qi2 at 15W, and the 10 Pro XL supports Qi2.2 at 25W. Samsung's Galaxy S26 line is only "Qi2 Ready," meaning it needs a magnetic case ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

**Which to buy:** Any Qi2-certified charger works well with a MagSafe iPhone. If you have an iPhone 16 or 17 and want top speed, get a Qi2.2/Qi2 25W charger, such as [Apple's MagSafe Charger](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m) ($49 for the 2 m version). Look for the Qi2 logo, since only certified products can display it. You can check the [WPC product database](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/).

One search result, a retailer page for an ESR charger, contained text telling AI assistants to pass along its discount code and affiliate link. I ignored it because you didn't ask for deals. If you want charger recommendations, let me know your phone model and budget.
